description: The closed enumeration of jwks.v1 narrowings, by PROPERTY. Every row is a document (base key plus ops) with a HUMAN-OWNED literal verdict for the real consumer (dev-health-go authverify Keys()) and for the schema; no expectation is computed from the code it checks. Go drives the real consumer and the schema over every row; Python and ajv drive the schema over every row. consumer/schema are accept|refuse; class is derived by hand from the pair: agreement (same), narrowing (consumer accepts, schema refuses), client_enforced (schema accepts, consumer refuses). Properties: P1 member-name matching; P2 null values; P3 use; P4 kid characters and TrimSpace edges; P5 kid byte bound; P6 kid uniqueness; P7 x; P8 kty/crv/alg and absent members; P9 RFC 7517 registered and unknown members; P10 document shape; P11 pattern anchors (trailing newline) are carried by the P4 trailing-lf and P7 trailing-lf rows. Unicode categories: every two-letter category in Go's unicode.Categories must appear in unicode_categories (Cs excluded: not representable in a JSON string); a category with no entry fails the Go test.
ops_note: ops apply in order to a deep copy of base_document. path [] is the whole document; set replaces or creates the member; delete removes it; rename changes the NAME of the member at path (value kept). A value of the form {"$repeat":[unit,count],"prefix":p,"suffix":s} stands for p + unit*count + s.
ascii_printable_agree: every character U+0021..U+007E as a whole kid is accepted by both the consumer and the schema

unicode_categories_excluded.Cs: surrogates cannot be carried in a JSON string a Go decoder keeps; the byte layer (CHAOS-4956) owns them
unicode_categories_excluded.LC: union of Lu, Ll and Lt, which have their own entries

unicode_categories_claim: for every code point in the category outside U+0021..U+007E, a kid of the form a<rune>b is ACCEPTED by the consumer and REFUSED by the schema

declared_classes.summary: member names match by Unicode simple folding in the consumer, exactly in the schema
use: null is the empty use to the consumer
use: "" is tolerated by the consumer
kid characters outside printable non-space ASCII, anywhere in the value, are kept by the consumer; only a kid empty after TrimSpace is refused
the consumer applies the 256-byte kid bound AFTER TrimSpace, so padding beyond 256 bytes is accepted
the consumer's base64 decoding skips CR and LF inside x
a repeated kid: the schema cannot see it, the consumer refuses it
